data.long_meaning: The name Baraj is derived from the Arabic word 'barajah' which means 'thunderbolt'. It is a powerful and strong name that is often associated with the natural beauty and power of a thunderstorm. The name Baraj carries the meaning “Thunder” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Baraj usually hope their child will grow to embody thunder and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Baraj belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Thunder.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Baraj total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hawaiyal's Tarikh al-Buldan mentions Baraj as a city in the province of Aleppo, Syria, during the early Islamic period in the 8th century. It was a significant agricultural center and one of the main stops on the trade route from the Mediterranean to the Euphrates River.

Al-Idrisi's Geography of the World describes Baraj as a city in the province of Qinnasrin, Syria, during the late medieval period in the 12th century. It was an important market town and a center for the production of textiles, particularly silk.
historical_references.context: Market town and textile production center

Sustainable agriculture is a method of farming that focuses on reducing environmental impact and improving social benefits.
